checks.label: The order of operations still applies when negatives are included, so every screen's working does brackets, then powers, then times and divide, then add and take away, partners left to right, each row worth the same as the sum
Brackets are needed to make 9 negative and then square it, so (−9)² = 81 while −9² = −81; in the same way (−3)² = 9 and −3² = −9, the arrow to 9 turned twice or once
It is best to use brackets when squaring negative numbers: each square or cube of a negative number in this lesson has its brackets, and each power written after a lone minus raises the number alone

Equal partners go left to right: 8 − 3 + 2 = 7, while adding first gives 8 − 5 = 3; 1 − 4 + 2 = −1, not 1 − 6 = −5; and the times or divide goes before the add, so 6 + 12 ÷ −3 = 2, not 18 ÷ −3 = −6, and 1 + 2 × −3 = −5

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives: adding first, adding what is taken away, squaring the minus, reading a power as a times, losing or keeping a power's sign, keeping a minus, dropping a bracket, forgetting the opposite, working left to right regardless
In 6 + 12 ÷ −3 only the divide is accepted as the job to do first; the minus of −3 is part of the number, not a job between two numbers; the working gives 6 + (−4) = 2

The marker lands where the working says: facing up to add and down to take away, it steps forwards for a positive number and backwards for a negative one, so 1 + (−6) = −5, 1 − 4 = −3, −3 + 2 = −1, 6 − (−3) = 9 and 2 − 12 = −10

The arrow pictures agree with the sums: the arrow drawn to the part worked out first (5 × 5, 2 × 2 × 2, 5 − 8, 4 × 4), then one half-turn for each minus sign left: −5² = −25, (−2)³ = −8, −(5 − 8) = 3 and (−4)² = 16

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; putting the brackets on or taking them off plays out within 4.5 s; every answer's motion within 2.5 s; hops and half-turns start at least 0.2 s apart

Putting the brackets on or taking them off part-way through never pops a picture in or out: tapped 1.0 s or 2.5 s into the screen or into a toggle, and tapped again 0.2 s later, no part's opacity changes by more than 0.5 from one 1/60 s frame to the next
Every answer offered sits on its puzzle's number line, and the right one is never at an end of it, so the line gives nothing away
